specific_expectations.text: use language conventions and non-verbal communication
specific_expectations.text_html: use language conventions and non-verbal communication

elaborations.text:
Language conventions:  

  use simple declarative sentences and conjunctions (e.g., and) to explain their thinking, reflect, and problem solve  
  use simple interrogative sentences to ask a variety of questions 
  use simple exclamatory sentences to sustain interactions with other students and adults during group activities 
  contribute to whole-class discussions using a combination of sentence structures in their first language(s) and the language of instruction  

Non-verbal communication: 

  ensure they have the audience’s attention before they start speaking 
  use facial expressions that match the content of their message 
  use gestures to describe the size of an object they built 
  vary rhythm and tone of voice when dramatizing or retelling information
elaborations.text_html:

elaborations.text:
Different uses of numbers:

  to indicate quantity or cardinality: a student uses magnetic and sandpaper numerals to represent the number of objects in a set  
  to indicate ordinality: a student lines up toys and manipulatives, and identifies the first, second, and so on 
  to label or name: “My favourite player is number 24.”
elaborations.text_html:

specific_expectations.text: solve situations involving addition and subtraction to 10 using concrete materials
specific_expectations.text_html: solve situations involving addition and subtraction to 10 using concrete materials

elaborations.text:
Situations: 

  join problems: A friend has 2 apples. You give her 1 more. How many apples does she have? 
  separating problems: You have 5 apples. You give 1 to a friend. How many apples do you have now? 
  part-whole problems: You have 7 apples. Five of them are red and the rest are green. How many green apples do you have? 
  compare problems: You have 8 apples. Your friend has 4 apples. Who has more? By how much? 

Tools and strategies: 

  use five and ten frames, connecting cubes, rekenreks, number paths, or fingers to represent the quantities in the situation 
  act out the situation using strategies such as counting all, counting on, counting back, or finding the difference (for subtraction) 
  use one and two more/less  
  use the benchmarks 5 and 10
elaborations.text_html:
Situations:

overall_expectations.title: Responding to Art
overall_expectations.describer: As students progress through Kindergarten, they:
overall_expectations.text: respond to a variety of forms of dance, drama, music, and visual arts from various cultures and communities, including using their language and mathematics knowledge and skills
overall_expectations.text_html: respond to a variety of forms of dance, drama, music, and visual arts from various cultures and communities, including using their language and mathematics knowledge and skills

specific_expectations.text: express their responses to dance and drama
specific_expectations.text_html: express their responses to dance and drama

elaborations.text:
Respond by: 

  using movements 
  making connections to their experiences with dance and drama
  describing how dance and drama make them feel
elaborations.text_html:
Respond by: 

  • using movements 
  • making connections to their experiences with dance and drama
  • describing how dance and drama make them feel

specific_expectations.text: respond to texts and art forms from various cultures and communities through classroom drama activities and make connections to their own experiences
specific_expectations.text_html: respond to texts and art forms from various cultures and communities through classroom drama activities and make connections to their own experiences

elaborations.text:
Respond by: 

  using actions, words, pictures, or props to retell a story or represent a poem  
  describing their feeling about a character in a story 
  sharing how they felt, using actions, pictures, or words, after listening to First Nations hand drumming, Métis fiddle music, Inuit throat singing, a song in a new language 
  talking about lines, shapes and forms, colours, and textures after viewing paintings, textiles, sculptures, or illustrations
